trails.title: Cleansing Notes
trails.description: First rule: don't mistake an agave for a pineapple, especially as a snack.

content.text:
1. Agave

Handling Note: Mind your hands around the large leaves. They're sharp.
Practical Uses: Commonly used in brewing, medicine, and rituals. Its fermented sap produces pulque, a drink Mexicans call "the lifeblood of the land."
Exorcism Uses: Smear the sap on door frames and floors after a space has been "cleansed" to shut out any "unseen presences."

2. Epazote

No special handling notes.
Practical Uses: Aids digestion and can expel or kill intestinal parasites.
Exorcism Uses: After an exorcism, if "their presence" still lingers in the room, sprinkle some epazote. Let's just say it smells as "special" as it sounds.

3. Rue

No special handling notes.
Practical Uses: Commonly used to ward off evil. Can be worn on the body, brewed as tea, or sprinkled on the ground.
Exorcism Uses: The final step of an "exorcism," it helps with sealing against future incursions.

4. Copal

Caution: Make sure the smoke spreads throughout the entire room.
Practical Uses: A natural resin native to Central America, used in sacred rituals since the time of the Aztecs and the Maya. Now widely used during Día de los Fieles Difuntos as a medium to connect the living with the dead.
Exorcism Uses: As copal smoke rises, "they" find their way back to where they belong.

5. Rosemary

For the living only.
Practical Uses: Healing.
Exorcism Uses: If the "scene" feels wrong, or you're dealing with a survivor who's lost control, a little rosemary helps you find yourself again faster.

items.text: At dusk, the sun casts its last fading warmth.
Deep in the alley, a bustling little shop hums as craftsmen prepare candy skulls for the upcoming festivities.
Candy Store

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: Good heavens, Añil! Hurry up!

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: If you hadn't guaranteed you could finish the work before the end of the day, I never would've hired you!

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: All this candy needs to get to Diago's before tomorrow!

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Yes, boss. I understand.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: Oh, and Ms. Juárez in La Roma wants you to repaint their family tomb.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: Damn, I almost forgot! I need to go to Christina's to pick up some marigolds before dark.
The storekeeper dashes off.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: There are still more than a hundred pieces of candy to go.
The sun falls behind the distant hills, and the craftsmen begin to leave. In the dim candlelight, his shadow dances on the wall.
Then footsteps break the silence.
I like the candy.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: We use them to welcome the deceased to the land of the living, guiding their souls to rest in their homes once more.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The Aztecs believed life is a cycle.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Death is but one part of an endless loop, a reflection of life. And how we die determines how our next life begins.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The souls of the warriors who gave their lives in battle rise with the sun at the palace of Tlālōcān, singing songs of triumph.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And four years later, they will return to the earth as colorful butterflies and hummingbirds.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Can you tell me if that's true, Ms. Ramona?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You recognize me?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The children from the Morelos District call you "Ramona the Ghost Seer." They say it was you who brought back the soul of Ana's Xolo.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: To hear it from them, you are some kind of all-powerful wise woman hidden in the shadows, one who knows this city better than anyone.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Of course, others say you're from a well-known family of psychics, though it seems as if you've chosen another path.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: They're just stories, rumors really. I don't see ghosts.
Her reply is curt, yet casual. Her past is behind her. She evidently likes to keep it that way.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: What they call "ghosts" are just pneuma, or say, a kind of arcane energy fluctuation. They exist, but not as some shimmering spirits; they're more like a cool breeze.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But, hey, people believe what they wanna believe. Kids and adults too, I guess.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Everybody's got unfinished business with the dead, so they want me to see ghosts. They believe it. That way, they've still got a chance to say what they never got to.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Ah! My apologies, Ms. Ramona. You're right. It was nothing but wishful thinking.
He unconsciously lets his eyes fall on her Vigiles Bureau attaché badge. It holds no authority, but it sets the tone of their conversation.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: So, is there something I can do for you?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Yeah, I got a couple questions.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: These symbols, I think you might know 'em.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: An arrow, a bow, and a net.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: According to the Codex Chimalpahin, these are the gifts given to the Aztecs by the sun god Huitzilopochtli.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: It's got the emblem of the Turquoise Serpent Club, too.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Which is the biggest smuggling ring in Mexico City, controlled by that arcanist Pérez.
She tucks away the scrap of cloth.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Can't be too many folks around who know you work for him. But those occult paintings at his club had to come from someone, yeah?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But your boss's been acting strange the last few weeks, right? More cutthroat than ever. He's planning something big, everyone knows it, and an auction to the tune of an "Ancient Bloody Civilization" is the best way to start it.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Hm, then it is true. Nothing in this city escapes you.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: And should I presume this interrogation has been commissioned by the Vigiles Bureau?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The Vigiles? Nah, what do you take me for?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You think I shed a single tear over "injustice"? Think I care about your boss's little auction? Nah. You and I both know that arcanist gangs aren't to be messed with, and I'm not in the business of making messes.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: But strange things are brewing in the shadows.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: On street corners, behind people's smiles, in the boarded-up buildings.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The pneuma is stirring up all around town.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Hovering over the city like a shroud, echoing in every howl and shriek in the night.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Like nothing I've ever felt before. Who knows what'll happen if things stay this way?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: It's your arcane gift warning you about the coming crisis.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I wouldn't call it a gift, especially when you're born into a so-called "psychic" family.
She leaves it at that, unwilling to say more.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Look, I know you know something about these arcane murders. There's already been five of them. And it's gotta have something to do with these weird spikes in the pneuma.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That's how I found these symbols, left behind at one of the crime scenes.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: So, I wanna know the connection between the club and these killings.
She wrestles the question out, realizing she's about to step far deeper into this growing mess than intended.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: If they are indeed related, that is, if it truly is the Turquoise Serpent Club who's responsible, what will you do?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'm not paid to solve crimes. The Vigiles got plenty of investigators. If they can't figure things out, that's on them.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Have to admire someone willing to go above and beyond their duty.
A gentle smile flickers across his face, then fades just as fast.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But I must apologize, miss.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You know I work for the club. And you know that means I can't provide any help.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: That so? Didn't expect you to be so loyal.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: If I remember, you used to be a plain old pigment supplier, until Pérez started snatching up every artist in town. I figured you didn't come into the job willingly. Was I wrong?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: You're not so different from those other artists, really. Just a little more flexible. That's why Pérez gave you a longer leash.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: If they can prove Pérez guilty, the Vigiles will—

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I'm afraid it's time for you to leave. This conversation will remain between us. You have my word.
She rolls her eyes, though the emotion is as much directed at herself as Añil. Playing detective isn't in her job description.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Hm. Sorry for wasting your time. See you later.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The Day of the Dead is coming.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Please, take some decorations with you. I wouldn't have you leave empty-handed.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Heh. Quite the salesman, huh? Still making deals even now.
She takes the candle with a smirk and tosses two Sharpodonties his way.
The little house in her dusty, long-forgotten cemetery, the quiet of her coffin—a familiar place to unwind after work.
—Usually. Tonight, however, she'll find no such rest.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Ms. Ramona, you're back! How'd your investigation go?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: The guy you went to see—is he a friend, or one of your informants? I knew there was something else going on.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: What're you still doing here?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: When I said "Don't follow me," I didn't mean "Camp out at my place and jump me later."

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Oh, I know. It must have been one of your ghost buddies.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I don't have ghost buddies.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: *sigh* It's the symbols we found at the crime scene: an arrow, a bow, and a net. They're the symbols of a powerful smuggling ring.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: The Turquoise Serpent Club ... I know a guy who I thought was being forced to work for 'em.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I see, I see. Then, everything's going well, then? Ha, lucky us.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Don't get your gears all spun up.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: He seems way too loyal for someone who's got a gun to his head. I got nothing from him, 'cept this thing.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Take it. Saves you some souvenir shopping. Now beat it.
She tosses the candle to Loggerhead, who scrambles to catch it.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Wow! What's this?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Just a knick-knack.
She pauses, watching as the candle emits a clear sign of arcane fluctuation, no surprise to her in a cemetery filled with spirits, yet it forces her to think.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: Wait. I've changed my mind.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Huh?
Loggerhead has barely enough time to register the item in her hand before the exorcist snatches it back.
She places the candle in her palm and studies it closely. Then she puts it away.

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I take it back. He might not be as loyal to the club as I thought.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Ramona
items.text: I'll get you something else to take home.
